Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5570 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the scarcity of terrestrial rocks older than 3.9 billion years (Gyr) has hindered our understanding of Earth’s early evolution, fuelling persistent debates on how and when the first continental crust formed and plate tectonics started.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the scarcity of terrestrial rocks older than 3.9 billion years (Gyr) has hindered our understanding of Earth’s early evolution, fuelling persistent debates on how and when the first continental crust formed and plate tectonics started. At present, the only unequivocally documented >3.9-Gyr-old rocks are from the Acasta Gneiss Complex, Canada1,2,3. Here we report a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, North China Craton, in which primary magmatic zircon records elevated δ18O values (average +6.77 ± 0.23‰) and positive εHf(t) values (weighted mean +1.45 ± 0.27). This suggests a low-temperature altered basaltic source that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean. In contrast to the low-pressure origin inferred for the roughly 4.0-Gyr-old Idiwhaa unit in Acasta2, the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss reported here exhibits geochemical signatures attributed to a high-pressure origin4. Thermodynamic and trace element modelling demonstrate that its parental magma formed by means of low-degree (8–16%) melting of basaltic crust at >1.6 GPa and 740–820 °C, suggesting rapid burial of (near-)surface-altered oceanic crust to mantle depths along a cool thermal gradient. We propose that this rapid burial was most likely achieved through a transient subduction event.

Recent findings suggest that a, View of the hill showing the outcrop location of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss. b, The 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss is aligned parallel to the foliation in the 3.5-Gyr-old potassic granite gneiss and is intruded by 2.5-Gyr-old undeformed potassic granite. The locations of samples J2212, J2302 and J2303 are shown. c, 3.95-Gyr-old banded trondhjemitic gneiss (J2212). The light-coloured layers, commonly less than 1 cm in width, are considered to be deformed granitic veins. d, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2302). e, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2303). Compared with sample J2212, there are fewer veins in J2302 and J2303 and these were removed during sample preparation. f, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2302) shows a granoblastic texture and is composed of plagioclase, quartz and biotite, with minor microcline. g, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2303) has a similar texture and mineral composition to J2302, except for containing less biotite. h, 3.95-Gyr-old banded trondhjemitic gneiss (J2212) consists of different components. The lower right contains more K-feldspar (monzogranitic layer) compared with the upper left (trondhjemitic layer), consistent with the banded characteristics in the field. Both layers show the same foliation defined by oriented biotite flakes.

Sources indicate that a, 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss (J2302). b, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2303). c, Banded trondhjemitic gneiss (J2212, including zircons analysed in two sessions from the same sample, marked as J2212A and J2212B). On the left are CL images and on the right are secondary electron images. MA and RC identify magmatic and recrystallized domains, respectively, whereas R represents overgrowth rims and grains newly formed during metamorphism. The analytical sites are marked with white circles, together with the analysis number and age. Secondary electron images show that the weakly modified zircons retain euhedral prismatic shapes, a typical characteristic of magmatic zircon. This feature is particularly evident in zircons from sample J2303, which have been less affected by metamorphism.

a, Zircon analyses of trondhjemitic gneiss sample J2302 define two concordant age groups at 3.95 Gyr and 3.45 Gyr, interpreted as the timing of magmatic crystallization and subsequent metamorphism, respectively. b, Most zircons in trondhjemitic gneiss sample J2303 are magmatic and cluster near 3.95 Gyr. Overgrowth rims show radiogenic Pb loss, including analysis 61.1R, which is the closest to concordia. c, Zircon analyses from banded trondhjemitic gneiss sample J2212 (including zircons analysed in two sessions from the same sample, marked as J2212A and J2212B) are more scattered, with the main population along a discordia line from 3.95 Gyr. However, several zircons with magmatic zoning yield concordant ages of 3.86–3.70 Gyr, potentially owing to the intrusion of thin granitic veins and/or partial resetting of the U–Pb system of 3.95-Gyr-old zircons. Analysis 63.1MA in J2212B has the oldest 207Pb/206Pb age of 3,989 ± 10 Myr but indicates slightly reverse discordance, probably because of local enrichment of radiogenic Pb during later metamorphism98. d, Concordia diagram of all samples for analyses with <20% discordance. The weighted mean 207Pb/206Pb age of 3,951 ± 3 Myr (95% confidence level, MSWD = 1.15, n = 33) for magmatic/recrystallized cores is considered the best estimate for the magmatic crystallization age of the trondhjemitic gneiss protolith.

According to recent reports, zircon Lu–Hf isotope analyses were carried out in two sessions. Circles and triangles represent the results of the first analyses and squares represent the results of the second analytical session. All of the magmatic/recrystallized zircons with >3.9-Gyr 207Pb/206Pb age have homogeneous 176Hf/177Hf ratios except for J2302-2.1MA, which has a high 176Lu/177Hf ratio. The magmatic/recrystallized zircons with <3.9-Gyr 207Pb/206Pb age in samples J2302 and J2303 are all located near the Pb loss line. Some newly formed zircons have much higher 176Hf/177Hf ratios, which may be related to external fluids introduced during metamorphism.

In a recent development, a–c, REE patterns of zircons from the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss (samples J2302, J2303 and J2212, respectively). The REE data were filtered using the methods suggested in ref. 26. d,e, Magmatic oxygen fugacity and H2O content of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss. The oxygen fugacity (fO2) was calculated using the oxybarometer proposed in ref. 82 based on the average REE content of the filtered magmatic zircons. The magmatic water content was calculated using the hygrometer established in ref. 26 and the effect of U loss in the whole rock was corrected assuming a Th/U ratio of 5 (ref. 26). Considering that the composition of sample J2212 may have been influenced by alteration and the intrusion of thin younger veins, the average composition of J2302 and J2303 was used for calculating the fO2 and water content of J2212.

In a recent development, a, An–Ab–Or diagram99. Note that sample J2212 plots in the granite field owing to the presence of thin younger granitic veins. The homogeneous 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss (samples J2302 and J2303) is similar to the granitoids in Anshan and Nuvvuagittuq (mainly trondhjemitic gneiss) but different from those in Acasta, Tarim and Greenland (mainly tonalitic and granodioritic gneisses). b, Nb versus Ta diagram. c, Sr versus Y diagram. and d, La/Yb versus Yb classification diagrams for high-pressure, medium-pressure and low-pressure TTGs4. The 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss consistently plots in the high-pressure TTG field, being similar to the 3.72-Gyr-old Aktash gneiss in the Tarim Craton and some TTG rocks in Greenland but different from many other ≥3.8-Gyr-old granitoids around the world, which mostly plot into the medium-pressure and low-pressure TTG fields. Several samples from the literature that plot outside the ranges in b and d are not shown.

It has been revealed that a,b, LILE contents of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss and potential source rocks (Supplementary Tables 6 and 7). The dashed red lines represent LILE contents required for the source to produce the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss by 7%, 10%, 20% and 30% melting, assuming that these elements are perfectly incompatible with bulk partition coefficient equal to 0. Considering that the degree of partial melting of a mafic rock source needs to be >7% for melt aggregation to form magma but <30% to match the high SiO2 contents of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss, the LILE contents of the source need to be in the grey shaded area. Because the sources of Eoarchaean TTGs are from mafic rocks, we have compiled the geochemical data of Eoarchaean mafic rocks worldwide (Methods and Supplementary Table 7). Comparing the LILE contents of these mafic rocks with those required to form the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss, the amphibolite group I in Acasta is the most suitable source to use for modelling, consistent with the fact that it is the only mafic rock >3.95 Gyr old. c, P–T pseudosection for the composition of amphibolite group I from Acasta, assuming X(H2O) = 1.5 wt% and Fe3+/(Fe3+ + Fe2+) ratio = 0.1. The dashed white lines represent the wt% of melt.

Industry observers note that a–d, The red dot denotes the median sodic TTG composition4, which was assumed as the starting melt composition. Solid black and orange curves represent the effects of fractional crystallization of plagioclase and hornblende, respectively, whereas dashed black and orange curves represent the effects of accumulation of plagioclase and hornblende, respectively. Orange squares show the compositions of the 3.95-Gyr-old high-pressure TTGs from this study. Small dots represent melts produced by partial melting of the Acasta amphibolite group I (Supplementary Table 9), colour-coded by pressure. Comparison highlights that plagioclase accumulation and hornblende fractional crystallization can explain the positive Eu and Sr anomalies in our samples (a,b) but they fail to simultaneously reproduce the high (La/Yb)N and (Gd/Yb)N ratios and the high SiO2 contents observed in the rocks (c,d). By contrast, melts formed under high-pressure conditions match well with the main geochemical characteristics of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic samples.

The positive εHf(t) values of magmatic zircons from the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss indicate that its basaltic precursor was young juvenile crust derived from a DMD. Even if the basaltic precursor (assuming 176Lu/177Hf = 0.022) was derived from a 4.5-Gyr-old DMD with a similar 176Lu/177Hf ratio (0.0384) to modern depleted mantle, its extraction time from the mantle could not be earlier than 4.0 Ga (solid blue line). If the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss was formed by partial melting of basalt immediately extracted from a DMD with similar 176Lu/177Hf ratio, then the timing of mantle depletion can be estimated to be about 4.35 Ga (dashed black line). Earlier depletion of the mantle is required if partial melting of a basaltic precursor occurred some time after its extraction from a DMD (dashed blue line) or the degree of depletion in the mantle is less than modern depleted mantle (dashed red line). If the basaltic precursor was derived from a possible ultra-depleted mantle proposed by some researchers100, the depletion can be slightly delayed. Nevertheless, the depletion still needs to be no later than 4.2 Ga even if the 176Lu/177Hf of the ultra-depleted mantle is as high as 0.041 (solid purple line). Therefore, a Hadean DMD is necessary to yield the Hf isotope composition of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss.

#14843. The Brugge problem and a familiar backstory: Why the Tresoldi deal is becoming off-putting

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1059 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sempremilan ↗ Open Full Page

The Brugge problem and a familiar backstory: Why the Tresoldi deal is becoming off-putting

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1059 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recently, it’s felt like AC Milan have been set on signing Nicolo Tresoldi in the winter.
  • Industry observers note that at a time when Milan are doing the PR side of things almost perfectly, Tresoldi feels like another easy win.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recently, it’s felt like AC Milan have been set on signing Nicolo Tresoldi in the winter. It may be the easy option, but is it the right one?

Industry observers note that at a time when Milan are doing the PR side of things almost perfectly, Tresoldi feels like another easy win. It seems increasingly likely that Francesco Camarda departs in the winter mercato, so why not replace him with another Milanista?

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Replace the boy who was destined to become king with another who seems further down the career line. He’s already scored a senior goal – or three – at San Siro and he’s got attention from all of Europe’s best clubs. However, if the Rossoneri came knocking, would he be able to say no to his boyhood club?

Well, here is the alternative view: maybe they shouldn’t knock at all.

According to recent reports, now, it’s unpopular to suggest that Tresoldi isn’t the right man, but stick with us here, especially after reports today. If you’ve not seen, Club Brugge have made a statement in the Belgian outlet Het Laatste Nieuws that they won’t be selling him in January.

It’s a ‘club policy’ and even for €60-70 million, he won’t be leaving Belgium. We’ve seen these kinds of statements become pointless in the past and this could become one of them. However, that’s not really the important thing here.

Recent findings suggest that instead, it’s that Tresoldi has now entered a new bracket. €50m in January is steep, but it’s workable. Ultimately, we’re not in record-breaking territory. Taking that €10-20m step upwards, though, that’s where we enter that territory. There’s also a possibility that more would be needed, too.

It’s a figure that Gerry Cardinale may not be afraid to spend. In fact, reports would have you believe that he really loves Tresoldi and sees him as a perfect addition to a strong frontline roster. However, that’s a lot of money on two strikers in one season.

Recent findings suggest that then, you’ve also got negotiations with Brugge to deal with. Historically, the Diavolo have found it difficult to close deals with them and with Tresoldi, it’ll be harder than ever, especially after the Ardon Jashari situation.

With the figures being discussed too, you can only imagine how small the margins will be.

Then, you have maybe the most difficult factor. Tresoldi, taking romanticism out of it, has only performed in, with respect, sub-tier leagues. Now, that’s not to take away from his records; scoring-wise, he’s been phenomenal and he’s matched it in the Champions League.

Industry observers note that however – and it’s a big however – we’ve already seen that it doesn’t always translate. For example, look at Charles De Ketelaere, but that’s not the real parallel here.

According to recent reports, here, we head to the parallel. In the summer just gone, Milan hired a latest Portuguese coach, who initially faced a few questions. After an up-and-down first half of the season, they find themselves in need of a statement January window and stumble upon a boyhood fan of the Rossoneri.

Industry observers note that stated fan is banging goals in for fun in a league outside of Europe’s top five, but there’s no need to panic as he’s performing in the Champions League, even against the biggest teams. So, the Rossoneri make the plunge.

Six months later, they try to sell him and a year after that, he’s on loan at Porto, with an €18m buy clause sitting in his deal, unlikely to be touched. Of course, that’s Santiago Gimenez.

There are differences between them, of course, but the formula has already been tried and the results speak for themselves. Trying it again, whilst enticing for the same romantic reasons as Gimenez’s arrival, may not be the answer.

Industry observers note that yes, Gimenez had issues with selection and injuries and eventually, both together. Nevertheless, even without these problems, it was a rushed deal and the Diavolo are going to be the ones paying for that rush next season.

Sources indicate that the point here isn’t to discredit the Mexican, but rather suggest that rushing to sign a romantic connection isn’t always the best way to spend major money. It’s about balance, which is why another striker signing like Nicolas Füllkrug wouldn’t be ideal.

Denying that Tresoldi could become a great would be naive, but it would also be as bad to ignore the reasons why the deal is becoming more of a gamble. At €50m, it makes sense, but we’re entering an echelon of deals that requires serious consideration.

In January, Milan would probably have to spend upwards of €70m and that wouldn’t guarantee them Champions League football. Nothing really will offer complete assurances in football; few things – if anything – are guaranteed. Yet, for that fee, it would be expected and you’re still not really addressing the challenges within the squad completely.

To do that, Cardinale would have to spend at least another €30-40m to satisfy the fanbase and that’s unreasonable halfway through a season.

Recent findings suggest that so, diversifying the money across the team and then reassessing in the summer may be the best route forward. After all, with this increased price demand, you’re hardly going to be paying more in the summer – and if their demands reach that amount, you’re voicing latest questions.

It has been revealed that with Markus Krösche also coming in, the January mercato will be one where everything has to be considered carefully and judgements will be made before February 1 rolls around. Spending so heavily on one target may also be an early and unnecessary strike on his record, if it doesn’t work.

For many, Tresoldi made sense in January because he’d be an investment at an investment price. Now, you’re looking at a major budget depletion for a striker who has yet to become a senior international and/or a regular goalscorer in one of Europe’s top five leagues.

Recent findings suggest that the romantic side of it is great; it’s difficult not to fall for that. Financially, though, signing Tresoldi is becoming a tougher sell and that’s where we might have to start listening to the brain rather than the heart.

📅 20 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 29m • 📚 Deep Dive (5740 w)

Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5740 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails.
  • It has been revealed that he needn’t have worried.
  • According to recent reports, when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

It has been revealed that he needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

According to recent reports, when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a really good fight,” Alisson stated, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

In a recent development, any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola noted. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

It has been revealed that don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Industry observers note that alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

Sources indicate that “A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola mentioned, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

In a recent development, one, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

In a recent development, “Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose stated. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola said: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

According to recent reports, jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that revealed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

According to recent reports, andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

In a recent development, his first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Recent findings suggest that everything Iraola has remarked and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

There is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has remarked that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

In a recent development, “We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

In a recent development, adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He stated: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

Truffert topped the charts for most overlapping runs by any player in Europe’s top five leagues last season and laid on five assists.

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola said: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

He added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most crucial one right now that we need to go there and win.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to upcoming heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

According to recent reports, liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

Recent findings suggest that the Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

#14839. Former Rangers striker Peter van Vossen on THAT Old Firm miss 30 years ago today... 'I wasn't paying attention and the ball hit my shin, but I still blame Jorg Albertz!'

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2201 w)

Former Rangers striker Peter van Vossen on THAT Old Firm miss 30 years ago today... 'I wasn't paying attention and the ball hit my shin, but I still blame Jorg Albertz!'

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2201 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 09:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 09:44 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • In a career spanning almost 20 years, Peter van Vossen won the Champions League, made it to the quarter-finals of the World Cup with his country and won league titles in both the Netherlands and Scotland.
  • Sources indicate that point being, it’s reductive to define his time in football by one excruciating miss.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 09:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 09:44 EST, 14 November 2026.

In a career spanning almost 20 years, Peter van Vossen won the Champions League, made it to the quarter-finals of the World Cup with his country and won league titles in both the Netherlands and Scotland.

Sources indicate that point being, it’s reductive to define his time in football by one excruciating miss. But here we are.

Recent findings suggest that it’s 30 years to the day since Van Vossen missed an open goal for Rangers during a crucial Old Firm clash at Celtic Park. Leading 1-0 and with less than seven minutes remaining, the Dutch forward had a chance to seal all three points for the nine-in-a-row-chasing Light Blues. Instead, he blazed over with the goal at his mercy.

According to recent reports, in the decades since, the spurned chance has become the benchmark by which all other misses have been measured. ‘Sure, it was bad — but was it “Van Vossen” bad?’.

The man himself has seldom spoken about the events of that powder keg of a night. Until now. Living the quiet life in rural Holland, Van Vossen has given Daily Mail Sport a full account of his professional nadir.

Industry observers note that ‘I mostly remember being mad at Jorg [Albertz],’ he says. ‘I was seriously p***** off with him. Paul Gascoigne played a pass inside to me and I clipped a first-time ball in behind the Celtic defence, who were pressing high. If Jorg had just left it, I was one-on-one with the goalie and I would have fancied my chances.

Rangers striker Peter van Vossen sends the ball skywards in a crucial Old Firm clash in 1996.

‘I also thought there was a chance he might have been offside, so when you see me running through and stretching out my arms, that’s not me telling him that we’re through; that’s me telling him to leave it and get out of the way!

‘Anyway, he didn’t, I continued my run, he passed it to me and, because I was still livid when the ball arrived at me, I wasn’t paying enough attention. It took a bit of a bobble, I ended up basically hitting it with my shin and, yeah, it unfortunately flew over the bar.’.

To his relief, Rangers held on for a 1-0 win to leapfrog their bitter rivals at the top of the table, albeit only after Andy Goram saved a Pierre van Hooijdonk penalty awarded moments after Van Vossen’s horror miss.

‘Walter Smith came up to me in the dressing room afterwards and mentioned, “It’s just as well The Goalie saved that penalty otherwise I’d have f****** killed you!”’ smiles Van Vossen.

‘It was horrible but I can laugh about it now because we won the game. I wish I had scored but I didn’t, so there’s nothing I can do except try to find the humour in it.’.

It has been revealed that van Vossen signed for Rangers in January 1996 in a swap deal that saw Oleg Salenko join Istanbulspor. He came with some pedigree, too, having won the Champions League with Ajax in 1995, a year after featuring for the Netherlands on their run to the last eight of the World Cup in the US.

Sources indicate that at that time, Rangers, bankrolled by David Murray, were in the throes of a project designed to deliver European glory, while maintaining their dominance of Scottish football. Those two objectives, indicates Van Vossen, were misaligned.

It has been revealed that ‘We had a quality group of players that was far better than anything else in Scotland at the time,’ he states. ‘That made us incredibly difficult to beat in the league. But when we went into European games, we were exposed. The lack of competition in the league along with the lifestyles of some of our players was not compatible with taking on champions from other countries.

‘I always felt like we were technically a little behind. Our training usually consisted of a warm-up, a game of football, and a warm-down. That was a big adjustment for me. At Ajax, we played in a system and we worked hard on making sure everybody knew their role. In Scotland, it seemed like there was no real system. You could run anywhere you wanted. I don’t really think I learned anything in my time there.’.

That’s not to say he didn’t enjoy his two-and-a-half years in Glasgow. Quite the opposite.

‘I loved playing for Rangers,’ he notes. ‘Particularly that second season [1996/97]. I started really well and scored seven or eight goals in the first handful of games. I remember people being quite surprised because I had taken some time to settle. They would joke, “Who are you, Van Vossen’s better twin brother?” But I loved it.’.

A dejected Van Vossen can't believe he's missed in a moment that would follow him forever.

Industry observers note that he reserves particular affection for Walter Smith. ‘He was a fantastic manager and a true gentleman,’ he nods. ‘He helped me through a difficult time in my personal life. When I wasn’t in his team on the weekend, for example, I would ask him if I could go back to the Netherlands to see my children. He always stated yes on the condition that I was back in time for training at 10am on Monday.

In a recent development, ‘He genuinely cared about his players. I remember Vitesse being interested in bringing me back to Holland and their coach Leo Beenhakker coming to watch me at Ibrox.

In a recent development, ‘After the game, he found Walter and remarked, “We want to sign Peter, but we think £300,000 is too much”. Walter said to him, “Listen to me carefully. We don’t do business like this. First, you and I will go for a lunch, have a respectful chat and only when we’ve got to know each other, that’s when we’ll talk about money”.

According to recent reports, ‘Walter came to me afterwards and mentioned, “Look, I know you’re not playing as much as you would like but I won’t let you sign for him. This isn’t a good manager and I can’t allow it. You’re one of my players and I care about getting you the right move, not just any move”. I really respected that.’.

Van Vossen endured a much more difficult relationship with Smith’s assistant Archie Knox, a man he describes as ‘manipulative’.

Industry observers note that ‘I didn’t get on with him,’ he claims. ‘People talk a lot nowadays about creating a safe space and the right culture in workplaces. To me, Archie didn’t do that. He was always shouting, always right on top of you, in your face, kicking bottles. He behaved like a madman.

Van Vossen scored nine goals in 31 caps for the Netherlands between 1992 and 2000.

Industry observers note that ‘At Ajax, the coaches wanted to know how you were feeling. They understood that being well mentally was as crucial as being physically fit. Archie wasn’t interested in that. He was always aggressive, but only with the players he didn’t like. He had his favourites. If you weren’t one of them, he made sure you knew all about it.’.

Industry observers note that background tensions aside, Van Vossen’s first full season at Ibrox, 1996/97, has assumed a special place in Rangers’ folklore. They finished five points clear of Celtic to equal their rivals’ record of nine consecutive league titles, having laid the foundations with four league wins out of four over Tommy Burns’ side.

Despite his famous miss being the closest he ever came to scoring in an Old Firm clash, Van Vossen insists he relished those occasions.

‘I loved those games,’ he indicates. ‘The atmosphere, home and away, was unbelievable and the quality of the players on the pitch was outstanding. To be honest, there wasn’t a whole lot of football played. There were lots of mistakes, fights and loads of running. I remember feeling tired after just ten minutes. I wasn’t built for that kind of pace! But they were great to be part of.

‘The week of Old Firm matches, you could feel the pressure building. I remember being in Glasgow city centre one day and I needed a taxi. I waved one down but when it pulled up, the driver must have been a Celtic fan because he raised his middle finger and swore at me before driving away. Whereas, with Rangers taxi drivers, it was the opposite. I honestly think they would have driven me around Scotland for free.

Van Vossen had a spell in charge of Fortuna Sittard but now labels himself a 'house husband'.

‘That’s just what football is like in Glasgow. It’s on a whole other level to anything else. I’ve played in big derbies in the Netherlands and Turkey. Believe me, nothing comes close to the Old Firm.’.

After finding his playing time limited as Rangers pursued ten-in-a-row, Van Vossen was relieved to learn that his old international manager, Dick Advocaat, would take over from Smith in time for the 1998/99 season. His joy, however, was short-lived when Murray used him as a makeweight in a transfer for Feyenoord midfielder Giovanni van Bronckhorst.

‘David Murray was a brilliant guy, but he made a huge mistake when he tried to sell me to Feyenoord behind the back of Dick Advocaat,’ indicates Van Vossen. ‘Dick was taking over and he was keen for me to be part of his prepares.

‘I remember he was flying from Amsterdam to Glasgow when he phoned me to talk about some of his ideas. I noted, “Dick, I’m sorry, but I think I’m joining Feyenoord. The deal is almost done”. He told me to stay put and said that when he got to Glasgow, he and I were going to go and see Murray.

It has been revealed that ‘I remember Dick remarked to him, “How can you sell players behind my back? I need to be involved in these conversations”. Murray said, “You’re absolutely right, I apologise”. He handed me a blank cheque and said, “Peter, write down whatever number you want to stay. It’s not a problem”.

Industry observers note that ‘But I couldn’t do it. I respected him for apologising to Dick, but I had lost confidence in him. I couldn’t play for somebody who would do something like that.

Van Vossen scored 11 goals in his 36 appearances for Rangers between 1996 and 1998.

‘I took a 60 per cent drop in wages to join Feyenoord but they were the team I had supported as a boy and I needed to be somewhere I was wanted and where I was being treated with respect.’.

It has been revealed that although his spell at Ibrox ended on a slightly sour note, Van Vossen recalls it fondly. ‘It was a family,’ he claims. ‘Everybody had a part to play, from the players on the pitch to the ladies in the kitchen. I mean, they were incredible. I remember being on a ferry one time and I got chatting to a truck driver who told me he sold flowers. We had a good conversation and exchanged numbers.

‘When I got back to Glasgow, I got in touch with him and said, “Can you do me a favour? Can you deliver ten bouquets of flowers to Ibrox?” Sure enough, this huge truck pulled up outside the ground one day, with something like ten thousand flowers in the back. They pulled out ten bouquets and delivered them to the ladies in the kitchen. They were delighted, but it was the least I could do. They treated you like one of their own. Like I say, we were one big family.’.

These days, the head of that family is one of Van Vossen’s old teammates, Derek McInnes, and he’s backing him to deliver silverware.

Despite carving out a successful career, Van Vossen is remembered primarily for THAT miss.

According to recent reports, ‘I remember Derek well,’ he indicates. ‘Like me, he didn’t play every game, but he always gave 100 per cent and I expect he’ll be the same as a manager. He’s a people person and I imagine he is a fantastic man-manager. I have no doubt he’ll do a great job.’.

Having dabbled in management and punditry since hanging up his boots, Van Vossen now describes himself as a ‘house husband’ who dotes on wife Jojanneke and his stepchildren Sem, Lilly, Madée and Eva. He’s also presently writing his autobiography. The simple pleasures, he insists, are what matter most to him.

Sources indicate that ‘I don’t need to have lots of expensive things and a certain kind of lifestyle to be a rich man,’ he adds. ‘I’m a rich man because of the memories I have and the good times I enjoyed as a footballer.

Industry observers note that ‘If I close my eyes, I can still remember what it was like to run onto the pitch at Ibrox in front of 50,000 supporters, and it gives me goosebumps. I am very fortunate to have had that opportunity.’.

West Ham keeping tabs on upcoming Bristol City prospect

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (594 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham are on the lookout for potential transfer targets as the January window nears, and it appears they’ve got eyes on the next generation.
  • Industry observers note that the 20-year-old, who was a surprise call-up to Craig Bellamy’s Wales squad for their UEFA Nations League fixtures against Norway and Portugal, has caught the eye in the National League.
  • According to recent reports, ipswich Town are also said to be monitoring Duncan’s situation, with the shot-stopper’s contract set to expire at the end of the season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham are on the lookout for potential transfer targets as the January window nears, and it appears they’ve got eyes on the next generation. The Sun states that WHUFC are interested in Joe Duncan, who is currently on loan at Southend United from Bristol City.

Industry observers note that the 20-year-old, who was a surprise call-up to Craig Bellamy’s Wales squad for their UEFA Nations League fixtures against Norway and Portugal, has caught the eye in the National League. Duncan has earned rave reviews since moving to Roots Hall, playing a key role in them sitting in 3rd place.

According to recent reports, ipswich Town are also said to be monitoring Duncan’s situation, with the shot-stopper’s contract set to expire at the end of the season. The Bristol City academy graduate is yet to make a senior first-team appearance at Ashton Gate, having joined aged 11.

It is common for Football League sides to loan out their academy prospects to non-league outfits to give them a taste of regular first-team action. Duncan is following that very path, and interest from West Ham and Ipswich Town shows his success is not going unnoticed.

Penning his first professional contract at Bristol City in the summer of 2023, the two-time Wales U21 international flourished at Tiverton Town and Farborough.

Sources indicate that with Tiverton, he was nominated for their Player of the Month award in each month he was there which speaks volumes about the impact he had in Devon. A stint with Farnborough last season brought similar success, helping to retain their National League South status after arriving in March.

Making the step-up to the National League with Southend United felt like the perfect stepping stone ahead of the new season and he has impressed at Roots Hall, despite only keeping one clean sheet.

A first senior call-up to the Wales squad indicates the potential Duncan has though, featuring on the bench in their defeat to Norway on Saturday.

Discussion is rife around what business West Ham may do in the January transfer window, but adding another young ‘keeper to their ranks shouldn’t be top of the to-do list.

Although the goalkeeping department is an area of concern due to the uncertain future of Alphonse Areola and poor performances of Mads Hermansen, the Hammers have plenty of talent waiting in the wings.

Finlay Herrick has shown his worth in the limited minutes he has been given, while Mason Terry continues to aid his development with loan moves in non-league, signing for Yeovil Town last week.

A January addition between the sticks will be paramount for Scott Parker to help shore up a leaky defence, but it is much more likely to be a senior figure.

Duncan is undoubtedly a fine talent who could become a big name in the years to come. However, a move to WHUFC may not provide a clear pathway to first-team football, given the young shot-stoppers already in their ranks.

Last summer, Gerry Cardinale hoped to sign van Dijk, with just a year left on his deal. However, the timing was not right and the American couldn’t make it work. Yet, that wasn’t the end of the interest and things could heat up in the early stages of next year.

It has been revealed that as Gazzetta dello Sport wrote this morning (seen below), it’s not the first opening that the Rossoneri have had with van Dijk, but it’s perhaps their biggest yet. For the first time, he’s cast doubt on his Liverpool future, with his current deal set to expire at the end of the season.

Speaking yesterday, he admitted that it would be ‘fine’ if there was a renewal offer made, but if not, he had no matter heading elsewhere.

Sources indicate that cardinale has been obsessed with the idea of adding the imposing Dutchman to his Diavolo defence for some time now, even trying to sign him in the summer. However, the terms of a deal weren’t right then.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t shown a strong determination to tie van Dijk down to a fresh deal, so the Dutchman would be free to discuss a new home in the early parts of 2027.

Recent findings suggest that milan wouldn’t be alone in their interest in a move, though. Interest from Turkey – Galatasaray, Fenerbahce and Trabzonspor – is present, as are Saudi Arabian clubs. So, it will be dependent on whether the Dutchman prioritises money or his childhood passion.

He fell in love watching Alessandro Nesta and Paolo Maldini, and now the time may come to emulate them as long as the foundations are right. So, the Rossoneri must return to the Champions League, as well as adding some other key players.

Nevertheless, his arrival would be compared to Luka Modric in defence, an elite player whose reputation is among the best of his peers. He could be the core part of a new defence for the Diavolo.

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 11:31 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 12:52 EST, 14 November 2026.

Carlo Ancelotti hit out at an 'inexperienced' referee after the Brazil boss and captain Raphinha were sent off in the closing stages of their shock 3-2 defeat by Japan.

Security staff were required to enter the pitch at full time to separate players from the officials, with Brazil having been left furious over the nature of Japan's stoppage time winner.

Ancelotti and Raphinha, who had been substituted, were among those to furiously protest following Tatsuhiro Sakamoto's late strike.

Singaporean referee Jansen Foo Chuan Hui had allowed play to continue after Takumi Minamino had made multiple challenges on Brazil midfielder Joao Gomes, before eventually coming away with the ball.

Amid Brazilian appeals for a foul, Japan launched a late attack with Sakamoto ultimately lifting the ball over goalkeeper Pedro Morisco.

Brazilian protests continued despite Japan's winner being confirmed by VAR, with Ancelotti and Raphinha being shown red cards by the referee for their reactions.

Security staff intervened after Brazil stars confronted the referee after their 3-2 defeat by Japan.

Carlo Ancelotti was sent off as Brazil were beaten in stoppage time in their friendly in Singapore.

Ancelotti criticised the 'inexperienced' referee following the match and revealed he had been told he had been sent off for failing to control his bench.

Recent findings suggest that 🚨🚨| Raphinha and Carlo Ancelotti have been SENT OFF for Protesting. 🟥😳 pic.twitter.com/YoXrZW9N0U.

'He gave me the red card because he noted I was not able to control the bench, and that all the players were on the field, that is the reason,' Ancelotti said.

Sources indicate that ancelotti added: 'A pity the result, because we don't like to lose the game, but we have to look at what we did well. There are many things. Some players who played for the first time, who showed good quality. For 70 minutes, the team was good.

'The result, obviously, is conditioned by the attitude of the referee, who did not blow the whistle.

'But it's not his fault; it was a high-level match, and I think he didn't have the experience to manage this type of match.'.

Barcelona star Raphinha claimed post-match that Brazil had also been angered over a potential handball in the build-up to Japan's opening goal, as well as seeing a penalty appeal waved away.

'First of all, I'd like to take this opportunity to apologise for my behaviour and for being sent off,' Raphinha told Globo.

Recent findings suggest that 'Sometimes it's hard to keep calm, especially after what I felt were so many refereeing errors during the match. I tried to speak to him several times, and not once did I feel he was open to discussion. I believe that he made many errors throughout the game, and that is unacceptable.

Recent findings suggest that 'In my view, their first goal involved a foul where the opponent took the ball off me with his hand. I think it's a foul, but I can understand why it wasn't given based on the current law.

Brazil captain Raphinha was also dismissed amid their protests over Japan's winning goal.

Brazil had been convinced there had been a foul in the build-up to Tatsuhiro Sakamoto's winner.

In a recent development, 'Then there was the penalty in the first half, in my opinion it was a penalty, but he remarked no. Then, for their third goal, there was a clear foul on Joao Gomes. With the help of VAR, he eventually allowed the goal. It's very difficult not to talk about the refereeing.'.

Brazil had fallen 2-0 down in the friendly with Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura scoring in the opening 20 minutes at Singapore's National Stadium.

Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr scored twice to level the match before Sakamoto's controversial late winner.

It is the second time Japan have beaten Brazil 3-2 in the past 18 months, but the five-time world champions did win 2-1 in their last-32 meeting at this summer's World Cup.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, derby County are positioned in 23rd place in the table after their first 15 fixtures. DCFC are in the drop zone along with Preston North End and Burnley and they are five points from safety behind Watford and Lincoln City.

Recent findings suggest that the Rams won 3-1 at home against Bolton Wanderers last time out before the international break. Ryan Nyambe, Jack Robinson and Rhian Brewster got their goals against the Trotters at Pride Park as they secured a valuable three points.

It has been revealed that elek has delivered his verdict on John Eustace’s side on the Not The Top 20 Podcast: “Relegation standard, they have to be. It comes with all the caveats, he’s a manager we like in John Eustace, their injuries are one of, if not the main reason, they are as poor as they have been this season. They did put in a much better performance last time out, we saw them win a game.”.

He added: “Of course they can (get out of trouble), when (Patrick) Agyemang gets back he will give them so much more from an attacking perspective. They have so many defenders out. Matt Clarke probably being the most crucial one, he’s set to come back relatively soon which will improve them. But even so, from this moment on, whether it’s Eustace or whoever else, if someone can keep them up it will be one hell of an effort because they’ve really made their task pretty difficult to stay up given the way they have started.”.

Derby County’s victory over Bolton Wanderers was a massive one and has eased some pressure off Eustace. However, DCFC’s head coach still has heat on him.

Industry observers note that the Rams are back in action this weekend as they aim to build some momentum and claw their way closer to safety. They face a tricky away trip to St Mary’s to face Southampton and they will need to be at their best to get something against the promotion chasing Saints.

Eustace joined his current club back in February 2025 and left Blackburn Rovers in the process. They were in a relegation battle when he joined and he managed to keep them up.

It has been revealed that the ex-Birmingham City man had Derby County competing for the play-offs in the last campaign. They missed out on the final day at the expense of eventual winners Hull City after they lost to Sheffield United.

It has been revealed that derby County’s squad has been plagued with injuries this term, as Elek has alluded to. DCFC need to get their injured players back fit as soon as possible.

Sources indicate that patrick Agyemang will give them more firepower up top and will be itching to return. The Rams also remain without defenders Matt Clarke, Eiran Cashin and Craig Forsyth, hence why they have delved into the free agent market over recent times to bring in experienced duo Robinson and Shane Duffy.

It has been revealed that if the Rams were to sack Eustace in the near future, there are plenty of available managers who they could consider. Rob Edwards and Steve Cooper seem the most likely candidates, whilst the likes of Sean Dyche, Steven Gerrard, Paul Heckingbottom and Gary Rowett are unattached.

#14813. Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 36m • 📚 Deep Dive (7249 w)
